newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila water project bids said still under process.
newsitem.headline: Manila water project bids said still under process.

text.p: The privatisation of Manila's waterworks is continuing and none of those vying for the contracts has been disqualified, a senior Philippine government official said on Monday.

The Asian Wall Street Journal reported on Monday the bidding for the $7.0 billion project, said to be the world's biggest water privatisation, had run into trouble and could be delayed by several months.

The newspaper said one of the consortia bidding for the project had submitted a technically flawed offer and that officials of the Metropolitan Water and Sewerage System (MWSS) were debating whether to disqualify the bidder or re-start the process from scratch.

"At this moment no conclusions have been made," said Mark Dumol, chief of staff at the Department of Public Works and Highways. "It's improper for anyone to say that a company is going to be disqualified."
The newspaper identified the flawed bid as coming from a consortium comprising Bechtel Corp of the United States, United Utilities Plc and Ayala Corp.
Reacting to the report, the consortium said in a statement: "We are extremely distressed at the insinuation that there could be a technical flaw in the bid submitted by our consortium."
The consortium, which calls itself the Manila Water Company, said: "...We have completely verified that our figures are in total and full compliance with the concession arrangement."
Dumol said the committee evaluating the bidding was scheduled to hold "clarification meetings" with all four bidders next week as part of the technical review process.
"These meetings are being held as a matter of due course," he said, adding that the decision on the technical review would be made public on January 22.
The financial offers of bidders whose applications are cleared by the technical committee will then be opened the following day.

Other groups to bid for the two 25-year contracts to supply water to Metro Manila include Lyonnaise des Eaux SA in collaboration with Benpres Holdings Corp; Anglian Water Plc along with Australia Water Technologies Pty Ltd and Metro Pacific Corp; and Compagnie Generale des Eaux with Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc.
The two winners of the contracts for East and West Manila are expected to invest $7.0 billion over the next 25 years to improve water and sewerage services.
